narr: Training, slow moving bands of flooding rainfall impacted Duval county and the I-95 corridor during the morning commute with a stationary front across the area and high moisture content. Flood and urban area Flash flooding caused some structure inundation, cars to be trapped in flood water and widespread road flooding.
ev: There was widespread street flooding with numerous cars stranded in flood waters across the San Marco, Downtown Jacksonville and Riverside areas. At 9 AM EDT, local broadcast media reported street flooding across San Marco. Street flooding and stranded vehicles were reported across Edgewood Ave, Post St, Willow Branch Ave, Beaver St, Kings Rd, Shircliff Way, Goodwin St, Gilmore St, E State St, Clay St, Duval St, Bay St, Hendricks Ave, Palm Ave, Naldo Ave, San Marco Blvd, Thacker Ave, Children's Way, River Rd and Landon Rd. Floodwaters were halfway up the wheel wells of vehicles. Multiple roads were closed due to flooding including Stockton Road near Beaver Street West and San Marco Blvd at Lasalle St. Multiple photos were shared via Social Media. About 4 to 6 inches of rain fell within the San Marco, Brooklyn and Mixon Town areas.

At 8:40 AM EDT, an NWS employee reported that there was extensive flooding on Philips Highway and Bowden Road. At 10:40 am, broadcast media shared that flood water inundated a home in Englewood and went up to the person's ankles. Widespread street flooding with numerous cars reported as submerged and stranded along roads or ditches. A swift water rescue was conducted to rescue a person stuck in their flooded car with floodwater up to their steering wheel. Multiple roads were closed due to flooding including Sabena Road and Bowden Rd at Richard St and Cagle Rd. Floodwaters went over car wheels or halfway up cars wheel base along Richard St, Bowden Rd, Barnes Rd, Kegler Dr, Revelstroke Dr, Philips Hwy, Reba Ave, Parental Home Rd, Spring Park Rd, Dean Rd, Belfort Rd, Putnam Ave, Vancouver Dr and portions of University Blvd.
